audits.mathematicalReason: The digits sum to 45. None of 4, 6, or 8 can be a one-digit prime or the units digit of a larger prime, so each must occupy at least a tens position. Compared with counting every digit at units value, these three digits contribute at least an additional 9(4+6+8) = 162. Therefore every eligible sum is at least 45+162 = 207. The set {2, 3, 5, 41, 67, 89} consists entirely of primes, uses each nonzero digit exactly once, and sums to 207. This proves both the universal bound and attainment.
